Compassionate, evidence-aware psychotherapy for people in transition

I blend relational, trauma-informed, and skills-based approaches to help you reduce distress and build sustainable coping. I work with adults navigating life changes, interpersonal strain, anxiety, and burnout.

{{PRIMARY_CTA_LABEL}} Sessions are private and confidential. Not an emergency service—if you are in crisis call local emergency services or {{PHONE}} if that is your only resource.

What I value in therapy

Collaborative clarity

We set focused goals together and test what helps, using measurable steps rather than vague promises.

Evidence-informed technique

Interventions are chosen with reference to research and adapted to your context and values.

Respect for your pace

You control the tempo. I offer structure, not pressure.

Myth versus reality

Therapy is often surrounded by myths. Below I separate common assumptions from what is generally true, informed by clinical practice and research.

Myth: Therapy will give immediate answers.
Truth: Therapy is a process of gradual insight and skill-building. Some relief can be fast, but durable change often requires repeated practice.
Myth: A therapist will tell you what to do.
Truth: I help you explore options and test strategies; you retain agency over decisions.

Representative case notes (anonymized)

Short summaries to illustrate typical paths work can take. Names and details are changed to protect privacy.

Case: Recalibrating after burnout

Client learned pragmatic boundary skills and restructured daily routine; anxiety decreased with pacing and behavioral experiments.

Case: Relationship communication

Through focused practice in sessions, the client improved assertive listening and derived clearer conflict patterns to address with their partner.

Practical details

I offer weekday and evening appointments. I accept private pay and provide superbills on request. For insurance options and current fees, see the Fees page.

Schedule an introductory session

Confidentiality note: Communications are maintained in secure records. Exceptions to confidentiality include harm to self/others and certain legal requirements.

Areas of focus

I primarily work with adults using integrative, research-aware practices. Below are common presenting concerns and how I typically orient treatment.

Anxiety and worry

Short-term skills (breathing, behavioral experiments) combined with sustained cognitive restructuring when needed. We prioritize interventions you can test in real life.

Trauma-informed care

Stabilization and safety are first. I draw from phase-based frameworks and somatic awareness for clients affected by earlier life stressors.

Relationships & communication

Work on patterns of attachment, conflict, and boundary-setting; practical skill rehearsal in session and between sessions.

Life transitions & career shifts

Decision-making frameworks, values clarification, and paced behavioral changes to reduce overwhelm during big transitions.

Burnout & workplace stress

Assessing workload, meaning, and daily habits; building micro-boundaries and restorative routines.

Depressive symptoms

Behavioral activation, problem-solving, and collaborative monitoring to reduce withdrawal and increase valued activity.

Common clarifications

I aim to demystify the process. These short clarifications help set expectations.

  • Timeframe: Some goals are short-term (8–12 sessions); others are longer, depending on complexity.
  • Outcome: I cannot promise specific results; we monitor progress together and adjust methods.
  • Privacy: Records are confidential. Required disclosures are rare and follow legal guidelines.

How I describe therapy to new clients

Therapy is an iterative experiment: we form hypotheses about what sustains distress, try manageable changes, and collect evidence on what helps. That pragmatic stance guides my work.

Start a conversation
Privacy reminder: Communications are kept secure.
Crisis notice: If you are in immediate danger, call emergency services. I do not provide emergency care.

Frameworks and structure I use in sessions

I blend relational attunement with structured skill-building. Below I outline the typical stages of work and the membership-style offerings I currently maintain.

1. Intake and orientation

We assess immediate needs, risk, and priorities. We co-design an evaluation plan to track progress.

2. Stabilization & skill rehearsal

Practical tools are taught and practiced in-session with real-world assignments to test effectiveness.

3. Targeted interventions

We apply focused methods (cognitive, behavioral, somatic) chosen for your goals and revised as data emerges.

4. Consolidation & transition

We plan maintenance strategies and, if appropriate, a stepped-down schedule for continuing support.

Membership options (current framing)

I offer membership-style pathways for ongoing support and periodic check-ins. These are described clearly so expectations are shared.

Foundations Membership
Monthly access — flexible slots
Best for people seeking short-term skill consolidation and monthly review sessions. Membership includes a monthly session and priority booking.
Intensive Path
Block-based sessions
A concentrated package (e.g., 6–12 sessions) for focused work on specific problems. Payment options and scheduling are discussed during intake.
Discuss a plan
Pricing and availability vary. Insurance is not billed directly for membership plans; superbills available on request.

Therapeutic tools I commonly draw from

  • CBT-informed experiments and thought-tracking
  • Emotion-focused exploration and regulation strategies
  • Somatic-attuned stabilization and grounding
  • Relational and interpersonal skill rehearsal

Frequently asked (different set)

How long until I notice improvement?
Many clients report measurable changes in weeks when using skills daily. Complex issues require longer timelines and iterative adjustments.
Do you use medication?
I do not prescribe. I collaborate with prescribers when medication may be helpful and coordinate care as needed.
Confidentiality: Records are kept securely. Required exceptions (harm, legal orders) are handled per law.
Crisis disclaimer: Not an emergency service. If there is imminent danger call emergency services or local crisis lines.
